peak_rss_note: Peak resident size counts the clean file-backed pages of the read-only mapping of the source. peak_memory_footprint_bytes is what the process held beyond that mapping. Both are from /usr/bin/time -l around the whole run, the two exhaustive Price(4) proofs included.

not_counted: A per-locate column also needs a stored permutation or ordinal to rebuild file order. That cost is not in its stored bytes: see permutation_estimate.

permutation_estimate.what: Per-locate streams rebuild file order from the locate of each message in file order. A store that keeps a file-order locate column, which re-serialising every message needs anyway, pays nothing more. One that keeps locates only as its partitions must store that sequence: at least its exact order-0 entropy below, in bits per message, with no context, or the fixed width of the largest locate.
